title: Supply chain & inventory
examples: What is the difference between buffer stock and safety stock?
Can a business survive without a supply chain?
How does procurement affect a company's profit?

explain.say: Today we are learning about managing goods in a business.
First we look at procurement, which means buying what a business needs.
Next we explore Just-in-time, which means getting goods exactly when you need them.
Buffer stock is extra inventory kept just in case things go wrong.
A real-life example is a bakery needing flour for tomorrow's bread.
The most common mistake is ordering too much stock when things are slow.

items: It takes up valuable storage space

faq.q: What is the main goal of managing inventory?
faq.a: The main goal is to balance having enough stock without having too much stock. This keeps costs down while ensuring sales can happen.
asks: Why do businesses count their stock?
How do I know how much to keep on hand?

faq.q: Is Just-in-time always possible for every business?
faq.a: No, it is not always possible because unexpected events like bad weather can disrupt the supply chain. Businesses need plans for these issues.
asks: Can I use JIT in a remote area?
What stops a business from using JIT?

faq.q: What is the difference between procurement and buying?
faq.a: Procurement is a much wider process that includes planning and managing the entire buying relationship. Buying is just the final transaction of purchasing.
asks: What does a professional procurement team do?

faq.q: Why do some businesses keep buffer stock?
faq.a: They keep buffer stock to protect themselves if a supplier has a delay or if demand suddenly increases. It acts as a safety net.
asks: When is buffer stock most useful?
Should I keep buffer stock for everything?

faq.q: How does a poor procurement process hurt a business?
faq.a: A poor process can lead to paying too much for goods or receiving the wrong quality items. This directly impacts profit margins.
asks: What are the risks of bad buying?
How can I make my buying process better?

facts: Procurement involves the entire process of acquiring goods and services.
Just-in-time aims to reduce storage costs by minimizing inventory.
Buffer stock provides a cushion against unexpected increases in demand or supply delays.
Effective inventory management helps a business maintain smooth operations.

quiz.say: A shopkeeper notices a sudden increase in demand for umbrellas due to rain forecasts. What action is best?

options.show: Changing the price of umbrellas to make more money.
options.say: Changing the price of umbrellas to make more money.

options.show: Waiting until the rain starts to order more.
options.say: Waiting until the rain starts to order more.

quiz.why: This uses the safety stock to meet unexpected, high demand without stopping sales.

wrong.0: Price changes do not solve the physical problem of not having enough items to sell.
wrong.2: This would make the shop unable to sell umbrellas when people need them most.
wrong.3: This is too risky because the delay might cause a stockout when demand is highest.

quiz.say: A manufacturer wants to reduce waste and holding costs by only receiving parts the day they are needed for assembly. Which system should they use?
quiz.why: JIT is specifically designed to match supply arrival perfectly with the moment production requires the item.

wrong.1: This defeats the purpose of JIT because it requires storing excess items.
wrong.2: Budget size does not control the timing of the physical delivery of components.
wrong.3: While helpful, local sourcing alone does not guarantee the precise timing required by JIT.

quiz.say: A company needs to negotiate better terms and prices for its main raw materials. Which core business function should they focus on improving?
quiz.why: Procurement is the function responsible for managing supplier relationships and negotiating the best buying terms.

wrong.0: Sales trends show demand, but procurement handles the actual buying and negotiating of supply.
wrong.2: This is a physical inventory action, not a process for negotiating better prices.
wrong.3: JIT deals with timing, but the negotiation of the price itself is part of procurement.
